intro: Louisiana runs its elections parish by parish, through each parish registrar of voters and clerk of court.

id_rule.text: Bring a photo ID with your signature, or a U.S. military ID with your name and picture. If you do not have one, you can vote by signing an affidavit after answering questions to confirm who you are. You can also get a free Louisiana special ID card from the Office of Motor Vehicles.

dates.label: Absentee ballot request deadline
dates.detail: Your request must reach the registrar of voters by 4:30 pm. You can ask online through the Voter Portal or in writing through your Registrar of Voters office. Different dates apply to military and overseas voters.

dates.label: Mail ballot return deadline
dates.detail: The registrar of voters must receive your voted absentee ballot by 4:30 pm on this date, the day before Election Day. Different dates apply to military and overseas voters.

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 6 am to 8 pm. Anyone in line at 8 pm has the right to vote.
